title: Continuous Euclidean functions have bounded norm on compact subsets
statement: Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field] with its usual Euclidean structures. Let $m,r\geq0$ be integers, $K\subseteq\mathbf R^m$ compact, and $f:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R^r$ continuous on $K$ for the subspace topology. Then there exists $C\in\mathbf R$ such that $\|f(z)\|\leq C$ for every $z\in K$. Empty $K$ and $r=0$ are allowed.
